question.text: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> accuracy. The time for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn></math> oscillations was measured to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn></math> seconds with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi><mo>%</mo></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
Time period of a simple pendulum is given by, T=2πlg.

⇒g=4π2lT2

Therefore, fractional error will be

Δgg=Δll+2ΔTT

=0.220+2140

=1.220

Percentage change =1.220×100=6%
